title: Lamb Rogan Josh
subtitle: Kashmiri slow-braised lamb in a deep red sauce
excerpt: Lamb shoulder braised in a richly spiced Kashmiri sauce with whole spices, yoghurt, and a deep red colour from Kashmiri chilli. Slow cooking is essential, the sauce builds from the rendered fat and braising liquid.

recipe.sourceNotes: Rogan josh is a Kashmiri curry whose name is typically translated as red (rogan) juice or fire (josh). It arrived in Kashmir via Persian-influenced Mughal cooking in the sixteenth century. The defining characteristics are the deep red colour from Kashmiri chilli, not particularly hot, and the absence of onion in the original preparation, which uses asafoetida instead. British-Indian restaurant versions typically include onion; this is a middle-ground version.

content.text: Rogan josh gets its colour and mild heat from Kashmiri chilli, which is quite different to ordinary red chilli. The sauce builds from yoghurt and the lamb's own rendered fat rather than from a tomato base. If you can find lamb shoulder with the bone in, use it, the bones add depth to the braising liquid. The dish improves significantly if made the day before and reheated.
Heat the ghee in a heavy pot over high heat. Brown the lamb pieces well in batches, 4 to 5 minutes per batch. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add the whole spices (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay) and fry for 1 minute. Add the onion and cook for 15 minutes until deeply golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes. Add the ground spices and stir for 1 minute. Add the yoghurt a tablespoon at a time, stirring between each addition so it does not split.

Return the lamb and any juices. Add 200 ml water and salt. Bring to a simmer, cover tightly, and cook on a very low heat for 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender. Check every 30 minutes and add a splash of water if needed to prevent catching.
Taste for salt and stir in the garam masala. Scatter with fresh coriander and serve with basmati rice or naan.
